query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating 0.5 wt% TiC nanoparticles into AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock for continuous‐wave laser powder‐bed fusion will act as heterogeneous nucleation sites, refine the melt‐pool microstructure, reduce residual tensile stresses, and broaden the stable processing window, yielding improved mechanical properties and lower processing complexity compared to unmodified powder under conventional CW‐LPBF conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Pre‐alloyed AlCrFeNiSi spherical powder (D50≈40 μm), no inoculants, standard flowability.
generation.intervention: Uniformly coat AlCrFeNiSi powder with 0.5 wt% TiC nanoparticles (<100 nm) prior to LPBF.
generation.conditions: CW‐LPBF in Ar atmosphere, laser power 200 W, scan speed 1200 mm/s, hatch 80 μm, layer thickness 40 μm, substrate preheat 200 °C; fabricate miniature tensile bars (0.5×0.5 mm cross‐section, 30 mm gauge length).
generation.structural_mediator: TiC nanoparticles acting as heterogeneous nucleation sites in the solidifying melt pool.
generation.mechanism: Nanoparticle‐driven increase in nucleation density yields a fine equiaxed grain structure, reducing thermal gradients and tensile residual stresses, stabilizing the melt pool (fewer spatter events), and raising strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Average grain size decreases from ~20 μm to ~5 μm; residual tensile stress reduced by ~30%; yield strength increased by ~15%; spatter events reduced by ~40%; allowable scan speed window expands by ~25%.
generation.baseline: Identical CW‐LPBF run on unmodified AlCrFeNiSi powder under the same parameters.
generation.boundary: Miniature components ≤10 mm; TiC loading 0.3–0.7 wt%; laser power 180–220 W; scan speed 1000–1500 mm/s.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—mechanism supported by analogous results in Al alloys and other HEAs but not yet directly in AlCrFeNiSi.

falsification_experiment.design: Print two sets of mini tensile bars under identical CW‐LPBF parameters, one with 0.5 wt% TiC‐coated powder and one without. Use high‐speed video to count spatter events in situ, then section specimens for SEM‐EBSD grain‐size analysis, XRD residual‐stress measurement, and micro‐tensile testing.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if inoculated samples fail to show ≥10% grain‐size reduction, ≥10% residual‐stress reduction, ≥5% yield‐strength increase, or ≥20% spatter‐event reduction compared to baseline.
